extracted.intended_audience: domestic producers (and associations) filing certifications to receive CDSOA distributions; legal/financial officers preparing/supporting such certifications
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards for domestic producers (or associations) to submit certifications claiming distributions under the Continued Dumping and Subsidy Offset Act (CDSOA), including required statements, recordkeeping, review, verification, and consequences of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing other orders/findings claiming same qualifying expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each certification must list all the other orders or findings where the producer is claiming the same qualifying expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a producer uses the same qualifying expenditures as the basis for distribution in multiple certifications, every certification must list all other orders/findings where those expenditures are claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer operational status and continued production
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification must include information as to whether the domestic producer remains in operation at the time the certifications are filed and continues to produce the product covered by the particular order or finding under which the distribution is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a domestic producer is no longer in operation, or no longer produces the product covered by the order or finding, the producer will not be considered an affected domestic producer entitled to receive a distribution (see 19 U.S.C. 1675c(b)(1) and 19 CFR 159.63(b)(3)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of acquisitions by opposing or related parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The domestic producer must state whether it has been acquired by a company that opposed the investigation or was acquired by a business related to a company that opposed the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a domestic producer has been so acquired, the producer will not be considered an affected domestic producer entitled to receive a distribution. CBP may withhold funds corresponding to the claimant's alleged pro rata share pending resolution of legal issues that may affect eligibility (see 19 U.S.C. 1675c(b)(5) and 19 CFR 159.63(b)(3)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized execution and statement under penalty of law; records assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification must be executed and dated by a party legally authorized to bind the domestic producer and must state that the information contained in the certification is true and accurate to the best of the certifier's knowledge and belief under penalty of law, and that the domestic producer has records to support the qualifying expenditures being claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must be signed by an authorized representative (printed page 28942). See the 'Verification of Certification' section for recordkeeping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overpayments are recoverable and collection tools
rubrics_metrics.description: All overpayments to affected domestic producers are recoverable by CBP, and CBP reserves the right to use all available collection tools to recover overpayments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collection tools include but are not limited to garnishments, court orders, administrative offset, enrollment in the Treasury Offset Program, and/or offset of tax refund payments (19 CFR 159.64(b)(3)). Overpayments may result from reliquidations, court actions, settlements, insufficient verification, administrative errors, etc. Claimants may wish to set aside funds and submission/negotiation of distribution checks is considered acknowledgement of obligation to return funds upon demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and correction timing and process
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification received within 60 calendar days after publication of the notice may, at CBP's sole discretion, be subject to review before acceptance to ensure informational requirements are complied with and amounts appear correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certification found to be materially incorrect or incomplete will be returned to the domestic producer within 15 business days after the close of the 60-calendar-day filing period (19 CFR 159.63(c)). CBP will not speculate as to the reason for the error. CBP must receive a corrected certification from the domestic producer and/or an association filing on behalf of an association member within 10 business days from the date of the original denial letter; failure to receive a corrected certification within 10 business days will result in denial. It is the producer's sole responsibility to ensure certifications are correct, complete, and accurate; failure may result in denial of distribution and/or demand for return of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and records retention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifications are subject to CBP verification; the burden remains on each claimant to fully substantiate all elements of its certification and maintain records to support claims for five years after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may be required to provide copies of additional records for further review (19 CFR 159.63(d)). Records must demonstrate that each qualifying expenditure enumerated in the certification was actually incurred and must support how the expenditures are related to production of the product covered by the order or finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing verification or submitting false information
rubrics_metrics.description: If CBP later seeks verification and sufficient supporting documentation is not provided as determined by CBP, amounts paid are recoverable as an overpayment; submission of false statements, documents, or records may give rise to liability under the False Claims Act and/or criminal prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP reserves the right to use all available collection tools to recover overpayments. Submission and negotiation of distribution checks is treated as acceptance of the obligation to return funds upon demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of claimant identity and amounts; proprietary claims risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the claimant, the total dollar amount claimed on the certification, and the total dollar amount that CBP actually disburses to that affected domestic producer will be available for disclosure to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of the certification is construed as understanding and acceptance that this information will be disclosed and as a waiver of any right to privacy or non-disclosure (19 CFR 159.63(e)). A statement in a certification that this information is proprietary and exempt from disclosure may result in CBP's rejection of the certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBP discretion to initiate and conduct investigations from public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Although CBP will accept comments and information from the public and other domestic producers, CBP retains complete discretion regarding the initiation and conduct of investigations stemming from such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of public submissions does not compel CBP to initiate verification or an investigation; CBP exercises discretion in whether and how to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: List inclusion does not guarantee entitlement; alternative basis required if not listed
rubrics_metrics.description: The published list of antidumping/countervailing duty orders or findings and associated affected domestic producers identifies parties potentially eligible to receive an offset, but appearance on the list is not a guarantee of distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic producers not on the list must allege another basis for eligibility in their certification.
